title: A Southeast US annual community fit reduced later error with HadISST but increased it with ERSST in 2006-2017
abstract: We tested early temperature fits on later annual changes in thermal community indices in four US trawl regions. Fits used pairs ending before 2005. Tests used adjacent pairs within 2005-2019, or to 2017 in Southeast US. With HadISST, mean squared error fell by 25% in Northeast US fall and 54% in Southeast US fall, but rose by 26% in Eastern Bering Sea and 93% in Gulf of Mexico. Southeast error rose by 30% with ERSST. Its HadISST gain was uncertain when early fitting uncertainty was included. All four joint intervals with a four-comparison allowance crossed zero. Fixed survey strata, area weights and record checks reduce some observation bias. Full-record index construction, short records, catchability and surface temperature limit inference. This is conditional transfer with observed temperature, not a prospective forecast or a causal climate effect. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and verified input retrieval are included.
